title: $d$-wave altermagnetism revealed by resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
authors: Guangkai Zhang, Yuehong Li, Xubin Ye, Vincent C. Morano, Sze Tung Li, Jaewon Choi, Rebecca Scatena, Shuai Tang, Maocai Pi, Mengqi Ye, Mirian Garcia-Fernandez, Alessandro Bombardi, Xiaomei Qin, Zhao Pan, Daniel G. Mazzone, Qisi Wang, Yi Lu, Yao Shen, Youwen Long
abstract: Altermagnetism defines a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order, featuring compensated magnetic moments with antiparallel spin alignment, yet lifted Kramers degeneracy without the need for relativistic spin-orbit coupling. Its ability to host spin-polarized electronic bands and unconventional chiral magnons makes it a promising platform for functional materials. However, experimental verification has proven challenging; while circular dichroism in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) has been suggested as a signature of chiral magnons, it remains controversial whether this effect is an intrinsic property of altermagnetism or an artifact of experimental geometry. In this work, we resolve this debate and provide unambiguous experimental evidence of $d$-wave altermagnetism in the strongly correlated Lieb-lattice magnet La$_2$O$_3$Mn$_2$Se$_2$. The RIXS spectra exhibit a $d$-wave-symmetry circular dichroism in the magnetic excitations that vanishes in the paramagnetic phase. Through RIXS-operator symmetry analysis and exact-diagonalization calculations, we prove that the observed dichroism is a direct consequence of altermagnetic symmetry constraints, independent of magnon branch splitting. Our results provide definitive evidence for the experimental realization of $d$-wave altermagnetism in La$_2$O$_3$Mn$_2$Se$_2$ and establish circularly polarized RIXS as a highly symmetry-sensitive spectroscopic framework for detecting magnetic phases that evade conventional probes.
summary: This paper reports definitive experimental evidence for $d$-wave altermagnetism in the material $	ext{La}_2	ext{O}_3	ext{Mn}_2	ext{Se}_2$ using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). By analyzing circular dichroism, the authors resolve a long-standing debate by proving that this signal is an intrinsic consequence of altermagnetic symmetry rather than an experimental artifact. This establishes polarized RIXS as a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing exotic magnetic phases.
main_problem: The study aims to definitively resolve whether circular dichroism observed in Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS) is an intrinsic signature of altermagnetism or merely an artifact of experimental geometry.
main_result: The authors provide unambiguous evidence for $d$-wave altermagnetism in $	ext{La}_2	ext{O}_3	ext{Mn}_2	ext{Se}_2$, proving that the observed RIXS dichroism is a direct consequence of fundamental altermagnetic symmetry constraints.
method: The research combines advanced experimental measurements using circularly polarized RIXS at the Mn $L_3$ edge with theoretical modeling via Exact Diagonalization (ED) calculations based on lattice symmetries.
model_or_system: The system is the strongly correlated Lieb-lattice magnet $	ext{La}_2	ext{O}_3	ext{Mn}_2	ext{Se}_2$, which exhibits altermagnetism—a magnetic order with compensated moments lacking relativistic spin-orbit coupling. The theoretical framework models two non-interacting Mn sublattices connected by specific symmetry operations.
key_observables: Circular dichroism ($\Delta I = I_{CL} - I_{CR}$) in the single-magnon excitation peak, which exhibits a distinct $d$-wave symmetry and vanishes above the Néel temperature.
important_parameters: The measurements are performed at low temperatures (e.g., 15 K) and involve varying incident photon energy, momentum transfer ($\mathbf{q}$), and azimuthal angle ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed dichroism is governed by symmetry constraints derived from the altermagnetic order, independent of magnon branch splitting or quasi-elastic susceptibility.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure and RIXS geometry; key figures map the momentum dependence and azimuthal ($\phi$) variation of the circular dichroism signal, showing clear $d$-wave anisotropy at low temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical context of altermagnetism, details the experimental setup using polarized RIXS on $	ext{La}_2	ext{O}_3	ext{Mn}_2	ext{Se}_2$, presents the measurement results showing $d$-wave dichroism, and concludes by theoretically proving that this signal arises directly from symmetry breaking inherent to the altermagnetic state.
why_interesting: The work provides a highly sensitive spectroscopic tool (polarized RIXS) to probe subtle magnetic symmetries in correlated materials, offering insights into how lattice structure dictates emergent quantum magnetic order beyond simple collinear models.
